title: The OpenPlanr delivery loop
summary: How a request becomes shipped code: skills you invoke inside your coding agent write plans beside the code, the planr CLI validates and syncs them, and review and operate skills return evidence for the next request.

nodes.label:
You
a feature, a bug, a question
in Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor
nodes.description: Every step is a skill you invoke by name in Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor. The agent never chains plan and ship on its own.

nodes.label:
spec
measurable specification
nodes.description: Shapes vague intent into a measurable specification grounded in the repository, asking only the questions that change the outcome.

nodes.label:
plan
stories, tasks, change lists
nodes.description: Decomposes the specification into user stories and tasks with acceptance criteria and file-level change lists. Plan ends with a Ship handoff; it never starts implementation.

nodes.label:
ship
one task, verified
nodes.description: Implements one task in the repository with the plan read first, runs the checks it discovers, and records provenance.

nodes.label:
land
release readiness
nodes.description: Assesses release readiness and prepares the exact landing sequence. It never merges, publishes, or deploys for you.

nodes.label:
.planr/ plans
versioned and reviewed like code
nodes.description: Specifications, user stories, tasks, and provenance, versioned in your repository and reviewed like code.

nodes.label: Source code and tests
nodes.description: Changed one task at a time and verified before the change is reported complete.

nodes.label:
planr CLI
validate · render · sync
nodes.description: Deterministic: stores and validates planning files, renders diagrams and reports, syncs trackers, and diagnoses installations. It never calls a model.

nodes.label:
Review skills
artifact · design · browser-qa
nodes.description: Artifact review boards, design review, and browser-backed QA against real routes, forms, and viewports.

nodes.label:
GitHub Issues · Linear
optional
nodes.description: Two-way sync targets. OpenPlanr does not replace your issue tracker.

nodes.label:
Operate readouts
evidence for the next request
nodes.description: A decision and action brief across seven executive lenses, built from what actually shipped.

accessibility.title: The OpenPlanr delivery loop
accessibility.description: You invoke the spec, plan, ship, and land skills inside your coding agent. Spec and plan write the plans under .planr/ in your repository; ship reads the plan first and implements one task in the source code; land assesses release readiness before you merge. The planr CLI validates the planning files offline, never by a model, and keeps GitHub Issues or Linear in step. Review skills check the change, and operate readouts return the evidence for the next request.
